In ASO contracts, fees are recognized as services are performed, while separate stop-loss insurance contracts (if purchased) generate premium revenue and corresponding benefits expense. 3. Value-Based and Service Contracts (CenterWell Primary Care, Home Solutions): - For value-based care, Humana receives a per-member-per-month premium, recognized in the period services are provided. - Fee-for-service revenue is recognized at contracted rates as services are rendered. Impact on Revenue Stability: - Government contracts, particularly Medicare Advantage and Part D, provide a strong foundation for revenue stability due to their size, structured renewal processes, and predictable monthly payments. However, revenue is subject to periodic adjustment for risk scores and audit results, introducing some variability. - Commercial contracts are shorter-term and subject to cancellation, which could add some volatility, but comprise a smaller portion of total revenue. - Minimum benefit ratio and rebate provisions, as well as risk adjustment mechanisms, ensure that revenue closely tracks the underlying cost of care, further stabilizing net income but limiting upside if medical costs come in lower than expected. - ASO and value-based contracts diversify revenue streams and reduce Humana’s direct insurance risk for those lives, providing additional stability. In summary, Humana’s reliance on government contracts with annual renewals and risk adjustment mechanisms, combined with diversified contract types (commercial, ASO, value-based care), generally supports revenue stability, though periodic adjustments and regulatory requirements can introduce short-term variability.
